name: ISM
description: Kubernetes-observable evidence for controls in the Australian Signals Directorate's Information Security Manual (ISM), September 2026 (OSCAL v2026.09.4) - https://www.cyber.gov.au/ism. Findings are partial evidence only; they do not establish ISM compliance.

controls.name: Non-root containers (ISM-1246, ISM-1604)
controls.description: Containers run as a non-root user and group. Running as root is functionality most workloads do not need, and it weakens the container isolation boundary.
controls.remediation: If your application does not need root privileges, make sure to define runAsNonRoot as true or explicitly set the runAsUser using ID 1000 or higher under the PodSecurityContext or container securityContext. In addition, set an explicit value for runAsGroup using ID 1000 or higher.
controls.long_description: ISM-1246: Server applications are hardened using ASD and vendor hardening guidance, with the most restrictive guidance taking precedence when conflicts occur. ISM-1604: When using a software-based isolation mechanism that consumes shared physical computing resources, the configuration of the isolation mechanism is hardened by removing unneeded functionality and restricting access to the administrative interface used to manage the isolation mechanism. Evidence boundary: A pass shows that scanned workloads do not run as root. It does not show that all ASD and vendor hardening guidance was identified, reconciled or implemented, and it does not assess the Kubernetes control plane, node runtime configuration or the administrative interfaces used to manage the isolation mechanism.
controls.test: Verify that runAsUser is set to a user id greater than 0 or that runAsNonRoot is set to true, and that runAsGroup is set to an id greater than 0. Check all the combinations with PodSecurityContext and SecurityContext (for containers).

rules.name: non-root-containers
rules.description: fails if container can run as root
rules.remediation: Make sure that the user/group in the securityContext of pod/container is set to an id over 0, or the runAsNonRoot flag is set to true.

controls.name: Allow privilege escalation (ISM-1246, ISM-1604)
controls.description: Regular containers set allowPrivilegeEscalation to false, so a process cannot gain more privileges than its parent. If the scan input contains PodSecurityPolicy objects and every one sets allowPrivilegeEscalation to false, containers pass whatever their own setting.
controls.remediation: If your application does not need it, make sure the allowPrivilegeEscalation field of the securityContext is set to false.
controls.test: Check that the allowPrivilegeEscalation field in securityContext of container is set to false.

rules.name: rule-allow-privilege-escalation
rules.description: fails if container allows privilege escalation
rules.remediation: Make sure that the allowPrivilegeEscalation field in the securityContext of pod/container is set to false

# regal ignore:directory-package-mismatch 
package armo_builtins

import rego.v1

# Fails if pod has container  that allow privilege escalation
deny contains msga if {
	start_of_path := "spec."
	pod := input[_]
	pod.kind == "Pod"
	container := pod.spec.containers[i]
	is_allow_privilege_escalation_container(container)
	fixPath := get_fix_path(i, start_of_path)

	msga := {
		"alertMessage": sprintf("container: %v in pod: %v  allow privilege escalation", [container.name, pod.metadata.name]),
		"packagename": "armo_builtins",
		"alertScore": 7,
		"fixPaths": fixPath,
		"alertObject": {"k8sApiObjects": [pod]},
	}
}

# Fails if workload has a container that allow privilege escalation
deny contains msga if {
	start_of_path := "spec.template.spec."
	spec_template_spec_patterns := {"Deployment", "ReplicaSet", "DaemonSet", "StatefulSet", "Job"}
	wl := input[_]
	spec_template_spec_patterns[wl.kind]
	container := wl.spec.template.spec.containers[i]
	is_allow_privilege_escalation_container(container)
	fixPath := get_fix_path(i, start_of_path)

	msga := {
		"alertMessage": sprintf("container :%v in %v: %v  allow privilege escalation", [container.name, wl.kind, wl.metadata.name]),
		"packagename": "armo_builtins",
		"alertScore": 7,
		"fixPaths": fixPath,
		"alertObject": {"k8sApiObjects": [wl]},
	}
}

# Fails if cronjob has a container that allow privilege escalation
deny contains msga if {
	start_of_path := "spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec."
	wl := input[_]
	wl.kind == "CronJob"
	container = wl.spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec.containers[i]
	is_allow_privilege_escalation_container(container)
	fixPath := get_fix_path(i, start_of_path)

	msga := {
		"alertMessage": sprintf("container :%v in %v: %v allow privilege escalation", [container.name, wl.kind, wl.metadata.name]),
		"packagename": "armo_builtins",
		"alertScore": 7,
		"fixPaths": fixPath,
		"alertObject": {"k8sApiObjects": [wl]},
	}
}

is_allow_privilege_escalation_container(container) if {
	not container.securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation == false
	not container.securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation == true
	psps := [psp | psp = input[_]; psp.kind == "PodSecurityPolicy"]
	count(psps) == 0
}

is_allow_privilege_escalation_container(container) if {
	not container.securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation == false
	not container.securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation == true
	psps := [psp | psp = input[_]; psp.kind == "PodSecurityPolicy"]
	count(psps) > 0
	psp := psps[_]
	not psp.spec.allowPrivilegeEscalation == false
}

is_allow_privilege_escalation_container(container) if {
	container.securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation == true
	psps := [psp | psp = input[_]; psp.kind == "PodSecurityPolicy"]
	count(psps) == 0
}

is_allow_privilege_escalation_container(container) if {
	container.securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation == true
	psps := [psp | psp = input[_]; psp.kind == "PodSecurityPolicy"]
	count(psps) > 0
	psp := psps[_]
	not psp.spec.allowPrivilegeEscalation == false
}

get_fix_path(i, start_of_path) := [
	{"path": sprintf("%vcontainers[%v].securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation", [start_of_path, i]), "value": "false"},
	{"path": sprintf("%vcontainers[%v].securityContext.privileged", [start_of_path, i]), "value": "false"},
]

controls.long_description: ISM-1246: Server applications are hardened using ASD and vendor hardening guidance, with the most restrictive guidance taking precedence when conflicts occur. ISM-1604: When using a software-based isolation mechanism that consumes shared physical computing resources, the configuration of the isolation mechanism is hardened by removing unneeded functionality and restricting access to the administrative interface used to manage the isolation mechanism. Evidence boundary: With no PodSecurityPolicy in the scan input, a pass shows that every regular container in the scanned workloads sets allowPrivilegeEscalation to false. If the scan input contains one or more PodSecurityPolicy objects and every one sets spec.allowPrivilegeEscalation to false, the rule also passes regular containers that set the field to true or omit it, so a pass then reflects only the PodSecurityPolicy setting. Init and ephemeral containers are not checked. It does not show that all ASD and vendor hardening guidance was identified, reconciled or implemented, and it does not assess the Kubernetes control plane, node runtime configuration or the administrative interfaces used to manage the isolation mechanism.

controls.name: Immutable container filesystem (ISM-1246, ISM-1604)
controls.description: Containers use a read-only root filesystem, so a compromised process cannot change the container's files at runtime.
controls.remediation: Set the filesystem of the container to read-only when possible (pod securityContext, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true). If containers application needs to write into the filesystem, it is recommended to mount secondary filesystems for specific directories where application require write access.
controls.long_description: ISM-1246: Server applications are hardened using ASD and vendor hardening guidance, with the most restrictive guidance taking precedence when conflicts occur. ISM-1604: When using a software-based isolation mechanism that consumes shared physical computing resources, the configuration of the isolation mechanism is hardened by removing unneeded functionality and restricting access to the administrative interface used to manage the isolation mechanism. Evidence boundary: A pass shows that scanned containers mount their root filesystem read-only. It does not show that all ASD and vendor hardening guidance was identified, reconciled or implemented, and it does not assess the Kubernetes control plane, node runtime configuration or the administrative interfaces used to manage the isolation mechanism.
controls.test: Check whether the readOnlyRootFilesystem field in the SecurityContext is set to true.

rules.name: immutable-container-filesystem
rules.description: fails if container has mutable filesystem
rules.remediation: Make sure that the securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem field in the container/pod spec is set to true

controls.name: Ingress and Egress blocked (ISM-1182, ISM-1416)
controls.description: Every pod is selected by a network policy that declares ingress or egress. Pods that no policy selects are reported. The check does not assess which traffic the policy allows.
controls.remediation: Define a NetworkPolicy, CiliumNetworkPolicy, or CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy that restricts ingress and egress connections.
controls.long_description: ISM-1182: Network access controls are implemented to limit the flow of network traffic within and between network segments to only that required for business purposes. ISM-1416: A software firewall is implemented on workstations and servers to restrict inbound and outbound network connections to an organisation-approved set of applications and services. Evidence boundary: A pass shows that each scanned pod is selected by at least one NetworkPolicy, CiliumNetworkPolicy or CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy that declares ingress or egress. It shows that a policy is present and which direction it declares, not that traffic is restricted. The policy's rules are not assessed, so a policy that allows all traffic in both directions passes. A policy for one direction is enough to pass. NetworkPolicy matching uses matchLabels and ignores matchExpressions, so a policy can be counted for a pod it does not select. It does not show that the allowed flows match business need, that the cluster network plugin enforces the policies, or that host firewalls and an organisation-approved list of applications and services exist.
controls.test: Check for each Pod whether there is an ingress and egress policy defined via NetworkPolicy, CiliumNetworkPolicy, or CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy (whether using Pod or Namespace).

rules.name: ingress-and-egress-blocked
rules.description: fails if there are no ingress and egress defined for pod
rules.remediation: Make sure you define ingress and egress policies for all your Pods

controls.name: Host PID/IPC privileges (ISM-1246, ISM-1604)
controls.description: Pods do not share the host's process ID or IPC namespace, so containers cannot see or signal host processes.
controls.remediation: Remove hostPID and hostIPC from the yaml file(s) privileges unless they are absolutely necessary.
controls.long_description: ISM-1246: Server applications are hardened using ASD and vendor hardening guidance, with the most restrictive guidance taking precedence when conflicts occur. ISM-1604: When using a software-based isolation mechanism that consumes shared physical computing resources, the configuration of the isolation mechanism is hardened by removing unneeded functionality and restricting access to the administrative interface used to manage the isolation mechanism. Evidence boundary: A pass shows that scanned pods set neither hostPID nor hostIPC. It does not show that all ASD and vendor hardening guidance was identified, reconciled or implemented, and it does not assess the Kubernetes control plane, node runtime configuration or the administrative interfaces used to manage the isolation mechanism.

rules.name: host-pid-ipc-privileges
rules.description: Containers should be as isolated as possible from the host machine. The hostPID and hostIPC fields in Kubernetes may excessively expose the host to potentially malicious actions.
rules.remediation: Make sure that the fields hostIPC and hostPID in the pod spec are not set to true (set to false or not present)

controls.long_description: ISM-1246: Server applications are hardened using ASD and vendor hardening guidance, with the most restrictive guidance taking precedence when conflicts occur. ISM-1657: Application control restricts the execution of executables, libraries, scripts, installers, compiled HTML, HTML applications and control panel applets to an organisation-approved set. ISM-1871: Application control is applied to all locations other than user profiles and temporary folders used by operating systems, web browsers and email clients. ISM-2128: The ability to install, load or modify kernel-mode code, including drivers, kernel modules and extensions, is limited to privileged users who require such abilities as part of their duties or functions. Evidence boundary: A pass shows that no scanned container runs privileged or adds SYS_ADMIN, across the namespaces visible to the scan. This is the Kubernetes translation of application control. It does not show host or endpoint application control, does not inspect binaries inside images, and does not assess host filesystem locations. It does not show that all ASD and vendor hardening guidance was identified, reconciled or implemented, and it does not assess the Kubernetes control plane, node runtime configuration or the administrative interfaces used to manage the isolation mechanism. image_in_allowed_list(image) if {

	allowedlist := data.postureControlInputs.imageRepositoryAllowList
	registry := allowedlist[_]

	regex.match(regexify(registry), docker_host_wrapper(image))
}

	not contains(image, "/")
	result := sprintf("docker.io/%s", [image])

regexify(registry) := result if {
	endswith(registry, "/")
	result = sprintf("^%s.*$", [registry])
} else := sprintf("^%s\/.*$", [registry])

  securityContext:
